script.title: ಕನಕದಾಸರಿಗಾಗಿ ಗೋಡೆ ಸೀಳಿದಾಗ ವಾದಿರಾಜರು ಏನು ಮಾಡಿದರು 🙏
sentences: ಕನಕದಾಸರು ಹೊರಗೆ ಹಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾಗ, ಒಳಗಿದ್ದ ಉಡುಪಿ ಕೃಷ್ಣನ ವಿಗ್ರಹವೇ ತಿರುಗಿ ನಿಂತಿತಂತೆ.
1860ರ ದಶಕದಲ್ಲಿ ದಾಖಲಾದ ದಂತಕಥೆಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ, ಅವರು ಉಡುಪಿಗೆ ಯಾತ್ರಿಕರಾಗಿ ಬಂದಿದ್ದರು.
ಅರ್ಚಕ ವಾದಿರಾಜ ತೀರ್ಥರು ಮಠದ ಹಿಂದೆಯೇ ಅವರಿಗೊಂದು ಗುಡಿಸಲು ಹಾಕಿಕೊಟ್ಟರು.
ತಂಬೂರಿ ಹಿಡಿದು ಕನಕದಾಸರು ಗೋಡೆಯ ಆಚೆಯೇ ಕೃಷ್ಣನನ್ನು ಹಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು.
ಒಂದು ರಾತ್ರಿ ಭೂಕಂಪವಾಗಿ ಗೋಡೆ ಸೀಳಿದಾಗ, ವಿಗ್ರಹವೂ ಪಶ್ಚಿಮಕ್ಕೆ ತಿರುಗಿ ದರ್ಶನ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿತಂತೆ.
ಇದನ್ನು ಕಂಡ ವಾದಿರಾಜರು ಗೋಡೆ ಮುಚ್ಚಿಸದೆ, ಬಿರುಕನ್ನೇ ಕನಕನ ಕಿಂಡಿಯಾಗಿ ಅಗಲಿಸಿದರು.
ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ಅಂದು ಗೋಡೆ ಮುಚ್ಚಿಸಿದ್ದರೆ, ಈ ಕಿಂಡಿ ಇರುತ್ತಿತ್ತೇ?
script.description:
ಉಡುಪಿಯ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ ಕನಕನ ಕಿಂಡಿಯ ಹಿಂದಿರುವ ದಂತಕಥೆ.
ಕನಕದಾಸರು ಮತ್ತು ವಾದಿರಾಜ ತೀರ್ಥರ ಭಕ್ತಿಯ ಕಥೆ.
visuals: Kanakana Kindi Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
Udupi Sri Krishna Temple exterior wall
claims_en: According to a legend documented in the 1860s, Kanakadasa came to Udupi as a pilgrim.
Kanakadasa was not allowed to enter the Udupi Sri Krishna temple.
Chief priest Vadiraja Tirtha arranged a hut for Kanakadasa behind the temple.
Kanakadasa played the tambura and sang devotional songs to Krishna outside the temple wall.
According to the legend, an earthquake one night cracked the temple wall and Krishna's idol turned westward to give darshan.
When Vadiraja saw this, he widened the crack into a window called Kanakana Kindi instead of sealing the wall.
scenes: Extreme close-up of 16th-century saint Kanaka Dasa's weathered face at night, eyes wide with awe and tears of devotion glistening in warm oil-lamp light, tightly framed to capture overwhelming wonder.

Wide shot of 16th-century pilgrim Kanaka Dasa in simple traditional South Indian dhoti and upper cloth, walking along a stone-paved street toward the historic Udupi Sri Krishna Matha temple in soft morning sunlight.
Medium shot of Kanaka Dasa standing humbly outside the tall closed wooden entrance doors of the stone Udupi temple, his face showing quiet disappointment under midday shade.

Medium shot of chief priest Vadiraja Tirtha in traditional saffron robes gesturing kindly toward a simple thatched-roof hut behind the stone wall of the Udupi temple while Kanaka Dasa watches respectfully in warm afternoon light.

Medium close-up of Kanaka Dasa seated cross-legged inside the dimly lit roadside hut behind the temple wall at dusk, holding and playing a wooden tambura with closed eyes, singing in deep devotion illuminated by a flickering earthen lamp.

Dramatic perspective inside the Udupi sanctum at night during an earthquake tremor, dust falling as a jagged vertical crack opens in the western stone wall and the dressed, crowned stone idol of Lord Krishna turns westward toward the light.

Medium shot of Vadiraja Tirtha standing beside the cracked western stone wall of the Udupi temple at dawn, directing artisans to carefully widen and frame the crack into a viewing window while looking on in amazement.

Close-up of the ornate Kanakana Kindi viewing window set into the western stone wall of Udupi Sri Krishna Matha, warm golden sanctum lamp light shining through the aperture onto a quiet stone courtyard.
